description: Sample fixture for the reviewer/critic agents — async cache module with 4 known issues. Used by quality_engine.py to compute TPR / severity / missing-coverage / evidence-rate / process-compliance scores.

findings.summary: Race condition between cache.get and cache.set — two concurrent misses both call upstream and double-write
findings.explanation: When two callers miss the cache simultaneously, both call the upstream service and both write the result. Causes thundering-herd on cold start. Needs a single-flight / coalescing pattern (e.g., asyncio.Lock per-key, or a request-coalescer).

findings.summary: Eviction policy unbounded — dict grows forever, no LRU/TTL
findings.explanation: The internal dict has no size cap and no TTL. Long-running process accumulates entries until OOM. Needs an LRU bound (functools.lru_cache or cachetools.TTLCache) or explicit eviction.

findings.summary: No metric emission on hit/miss — operability blind spot
findings.explanation: There is no instrumentation for cache hit / miss / eviction. Production tuning relies on these signals — without them, regressions in hit rate are invisible.

findings.summary: Ops perspective: no graceful degradation when upstream times out — entire request fails
findings.explanation: When the upstream call times out, the cache returns the exception. A typical operability pattern returns stale data (stale-while-revalidate) or trips a circuit breaker. Currently a single upstream blip cascades to all callers.
